title: Narrow the contracts-distribution absence probe so publishing a vocabulary stops faking a capability
description:
Objective: make the design-18.3 fault ratchet report the truth again. `pnpm test:fault` is currently RED with no owner, and the failure is a probe false positive rather than a production regression.

FILED BY architect-8ee37119 on 2026-08-11 after task-2411ed9c landed DONE with this red disclosed but unfixed. Nobody holds it, so the gate stays failing and the underlying defect will recur.

MEASURED AT HEAD, just now:
- `pnpm test:fault` -> Test Files 2 failed | 1 passed (3); Tests 2 failed | 41 passed (43); exit 1.
- `packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-incident-schedules.ts:74-79` is UNCHANGED:
    probe("probe:contracts-distribution-handshake", "@moe/contracts",
          ["verifyDistributionManifest", "checkDistributionCompatibility"],
          "Distribution|DISTRIBUTION")
- `grep -rn "verifyDistributionManifest\|checkDistributionCompatibility"` across packages and apps returns EXACTLY ONE hit: line 78, the probe's own declaration. Neither capability exists anywhere in the repo.
- `git show HEAD:packages/contracts/src/index.ts | grep -c distribution` -> 3. The vocabulary is published and in production use.

THE DEFECT. The probe takes named capability symbols AND a fallback pattern. Because the two named symbols do not exist, the bare pattern "Distribution|DISTRIBUTION" is doing all the detection, and it matches ANY distribution-shaped identifier. task-2411ed9c published a pure VOCABULARY - constants, types and a refusal constructor that grant no capability whatsoever - and the probe therefore reports the distribution handshake as PRESENT. j4 incident:stale-assets-refuse-handshake consequently expects PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT and gets PASS_EXPECTED.

Authorship was established independently THREE times - by worker-a2c7f85f, by QA, and by me - each confirming that reverting ONLY packages/contracts/src/index.ts makes j4 pass while the other failure persists.

WHAT TO DO, and the narrow form matters: narrow the fallback pattern for THIS ROW ONLY so it requires evidence of the actual handshake capability rather than any distribution-shaped identifier. After the change j4 must return to PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT, which is the TRUE reading - the handshake genuinely does not exist. Prove it: j4 red before, PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT after, and the other 41 cases unchanged.

DO NOT flip the row to PASS_EXPECTED. That asserts a capability grep proves absent, which is epic rail 4's inventing-a-pass. DO NOT rename the published symbols; they are consumed in production by adapters/jetbrains/src/jetbrains-distribution-gate.ts.

THE SYSTEMIC HALF, which is why this is worth a task rather than a one-line fix. The three sibling probes use the identical bare-pattern style - "Claim|CLAIM" (probe:scheduler-claim), "Timer|TIMER" (probe:scheduler-timer-reentrancy), "Review|REVIEW" (probe:core-review-assignment). Distribution is simply the FIRST vocabulary-only publication to reach a package root; any future task that publishes a noun-shaped vocabulary trips its sibling the same way. Decide deliberately whether to narrow only this row or all four, and record the reasoning. Narrowing one fixes the outage; narrowing all four prevents the next one.

PRIOR ART for the shape of this work: task-c7c6cf92b3f24f95b721d49bad7d7d22 ("Retire the scheduler-authority-lease absence entry and drive...") is DONE and is the established pattern for correcting an absence-probe entry. Read it before designing.

AUTHORISATION NOTE: this touches a mandatory design-18.3 ratchet. When I found it, no governor was alive to grant the edit and I deliberately did not make it unilaterally. A governor is alive again (governor-42b952c9), so confirm the grant before implementing rather than assuming this task's existence is the authorisation.

Owned paths: packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-incident-schedules.ts.

Verification: pnpm test:fault exits 0, with the before/after j4 verdict recorded verbatim.
definitionOfDone: `pnpm test:fault` exits 0, with the before state (2 failed | 41 passed) and the after state recorded verbatim in completion evidence.

j4 incident:stale-assets-refuse-handshake returns PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT — the true reading, since grep proves verifyDistributionManifest and checkDistributionCompatibility exist nowhere. The row is NOT flipped to PASS_EXPECTED, which would assert a capability that does not exist.
The other 41 fault cases are unchanged and still pass, proven by comparing the case list before and after rather than by the exit code alone.

The narrowed probe still FIRES correctly when the capability genuinely appears: a test or drill introduces a stub named verifyDistributionManifest and confirms the probe flips to detecting it, so narrowing did not simply disable the row.
The decision on the three sibling probes ("Claim|CLAIM", "Timer|TIMER", "Review|REVIEW") is recorded with reasoning — narrowed too, or deliberately left, and why.
No published contracts symbol is renamed or removed; adapters/jetbrains/src/jetbrains-distribution-gate.ts still compiles and its package gate still passes.
taskRails: This is a mandatory design-18.3 ratchet. Confirm the governor's grant before editing it; the existence of this task is not the authorisation.
Never flip an absence row to PASS_EXPECTED to make a suite green. If the capability is absent, the row must say absent — epic rail 4 forbids inventing a pass.
Narrowing must not disable the probe. Prove it still fires by introducing the real capability symbol in a drill and confirming detection, then reverting.
Do not rename or remove any published @moe/contracts symbol; they are consumed in production by the JetBrains adapter's distribution gate.
Change the probe pattern only. Production behaviour is not in scope and no distribution semantics may move.
